finding.claim: A urlencoded POST whose Content-Type includes parameters (e.g. '; charset=UTF-8') is never selected for urlencoded body parsing, so ARGS_POST is empty and ARGS-targeted rules do not inspect the payload.
finding.source: Raw Content-Type request header value, supplied by any HTTP client.
finding.sink: Body-processor selection in ProcessRequestBody (transaction.go:1100-1120); payload never reaches ARGS_POST.

trace.note: Exact equality with 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'; parameterized value does not match so reqbodyProcessor is not set

ForceRequestBodyVariable defaults to false, so no fallback parsing

finding.guards_checked: Multipart branch uses HasPrefix (transaction.go:388) so the two branches are inconsistent; ForceRequestBodyVariable default false (waf.go:210); only urlencoded test (transaction_test.go:1836) uses the bare header, so the parameterized form is untested. finding.claim: With two Content-Type headers, the body processor is chosen from the last matching header (overwrite at lines 387/389) while the MIME type passed to the processor is the first header value (line 1092), so the processor and MIME can disagree and the body is parsed differently from how the backend parses it.
finding.source: Two Content-Type request header values sent by the client.
finding.sink: Body parsing in ProcessRequestBody; backend parses the body under a different content type than the WAF inspects.

trace.note: Each matching Content-Type overwrites reqbodyProcessor; last header wins
MIME type taken as first value from requestHeaders.Get
If MIME is urlencoded but processor is MULTIPART, returns 'not a multipart body' error
Error only sets REQBODY_PROCESSOR_ERROR; ARGS left empty, rules still evaluated

finding.guards_checked: Rules keyed on REQBODY_PROCESSOR_ERROR (e.g. CRS) would mitigate; Go Header.Get returns first value so most backends agree with the MIME choice, making exploitation depend on backend or proxy header selection. Confidence medium-low. Not executed.
